reason: Registry duplicate-id detection lives at the loader layer. The TypeScript validate() is handed an id-keyed project in which duplicates have already collapsed, so the case is addressed to python only (see its expected.json); the Python reference sees the raw array and reports it.

Asset bindings are a deploy-time concern that lives only in the Python reference validator: the TypeScript project model has no binding entities and validate() never reads data/bindings, so the dangling-VO-binding warning is python-only by construction (the case is addressed to python in its expected.json).

Once two nodes share an id the dialogue graph is ill-defined. Python merges both copies' outgoing edges under the one id, so node_close stays reachable; TypeScript keys nodes by id and the surviving copy has no edges, so node_close is unreachable. The REACH warning is an artefact of the DUP error both sides report, and it disappears with the duplicate.

The Python reference validates rules.json against the published JSON Schema (whose dice pattern rejects '2x6') before running the RULES check, so one defect is reported twice. TypeScript parses rules.json with a permissive loader and reports the same defect once, from the RULES rule alone.

The seeded dialogue (dlg_extra, deliberately offer-less and effect-free) fails the schema on choice.whenLocked. The Python reference drops a schema-invalid file from every later rule, so it never sees the dialogue at all; the TypeScript guard keeps a shape-safe entity in the pass beside its SCHEMA error, so the OFFER coverage rule also sees a spoken dialogue that nothing offers. Both report the one SCHEMA error the case is about.

The Python reference checks every custom row id against the id pattern at load time (a row id becomes a filename and a URL segment), so '__proto__' is reported as not lowercase snake_case beside the REF the case is about. The TypeScript side enforces the pattern only when a row is WRITTEN (saveCustomEntities throws), never in validate().

Same layer difference as custom-entity-prototype-keys: the row id pattern is a load-time SCHEMA check in the Python reference and a write-time refusal in the editor, so validate() there says nothing. The case is addressed to python in its expected.json.

Both report the SCHEMA on the id and the REF from the dialogue that names the un-newlined id. The Python reference drops a schema-invalid file from every later rule; the TypeScript guard keeps a shape-safe entity in the pass beside its SCHEMA error. So TypeScript also sees a character ('npc_keeper\n') that no dialogue speaks and reports COVERAGE; Python never walks the failed character.

The Python reference validates progression.json against the published JSON Schema (integer items); the TypeScript loader has no zod schema for it and the PROG ordering rule compares 'a' <= 1 as false, so it reports nothing. Same layer difference as project-rules-bad-dice. Addressed to python in its expected.json.

skills.json with `"skills": null` is a SCHEMA error in the Python reference (the registry's array is not an array); the TypeScript loader reads it as an empty registry and validate() sees nothing wrong. Addressed to python in its expected.json — widen when the loader reports the shape.

data/types.json as an array is a SCHEMA error in the Python reference; the TypeScript loader iterates Object.entries([]) and declares no types, so validate() sees nothing. Addressed to python in its expected.json — widen when the loader reports the shape.
